'''''Iresine''''' is a [[genus]] of [[flowering plant]]s in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Amaranthaceae]].<ref name=POWO_327328-2/><ref name="GRIN"/> It contains 20 to 25 species, all of which are native to the [[Americas|American]] [[tropics]]. The generic name is derived from the [[Greek language|Greek]] word εριος (''erios''), meaning "[[wool]]y", referring to the [[trichome]]-covered flowers.<ref>{{cite book |url = https://books.google.com/books?id=NJ6PyhVuecwC |title = The Names of Plants |first=D. |last=Gledhill |edition = 4th |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-86645-3 |year=2008 |page=217 }}</ref> '''Bloodleaf'''<ref name="ITIS">{{ITIS |id=20814 |taxon=''Iresine'' |access-date=2010-02-24}}</ref> is a common name for those species that have colored foliage, and these are often cultivated as [[ornamental plant]]s. Some species are additives to versions of the hallucinogenic drink [[ayahuasca]].
